summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a router between two isolated segments: eth1 (172.20.1.1/24, toward node2) and eth2 (172.20.2.1/24, toward node3), with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. Configured node2's enp8s0 as 172.20.1.2/24 and node3's enp8s0 as 172.20.2.2/24 via NetworkManager static profiles, each with a static route to the other's segment via node1. Verified node2<->node3 reachability through node1. Persisted node1's config via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-antrieb-segments (auto-applied by SONiC's networking service, sourced from the stock interfaces template) and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf (applied at boot by systemd-sysctl). Restarted node1 with a native `reboot`, confirmed a changed boot_id after it came back (SONiC boot took ~4 minutes), confirmed eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls returned automatically without any post-boot intervention, and re-verified node2<->node3 ping succeeded with 0% loss in both directions. node2 and node3 were not restarted (task scoped the restart to node1 only; they were never disrupted so no restart evidence applies to them).
actions_performed: Surveyed topology and interfaces on node1/node2/node3 (ip addr, ip route, /etc/hosts, CLUSTER_HOSTS)
Inspected SONiC's interfaces-config.sh and interfaces.j2 template to determine a persistence-safe config location
Cleaned up node1's docker0 class-E address per SONiC gotchas and assigned eth1/eth2 addresses
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1 (eth1, eth2)
Wrote /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-antrieb-segments and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf on node1 for boot-time persistence
Reconfigured node2 and node3's second NIC (enp8s0) to static IPs via nmcli, with static routes to each other's segment via node1
Verified node2<->node3 ping success through node1 (pre-restart baseline)
Captured boot_id/uptime baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via `reboot`, polled until it returned
Confirmed node1's boot_id changed, confirming a real restart
Re-verified eth1/eth2 addresses, forwarding sysctls, and persisted config files on node1 post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 has a routed address on each of its two segments
evidence.summary: eth1 assigned 172.20.1.1/24 and eth2 assigned 172.20.2.1/24 on node1, confirmed by ip addr output

evidence.requirement: working path between node2 and node3 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: node2 (172.20.1.2/24) and node3 (172.20.2.2/24) configured with routes via node1; ping between them succeeded with 0% loss in both directions
Wrote /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-antrieb-segments (static eth1/eth2 addresses, auto-sourced by SONiC's networking service) and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf (forwarding sysctls, applied at boot)
Captured node1 boot_id e5168e03-df6d-4e9f-b014-5de4bdfa0688, uptime, eth1/eth2 addresses, and ip_forward=1 before restart
Issued backgrounded `reboot` on node1; command acknowledged before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of restart)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 5efc5171-0791-4033-b821-2efe1d991a3a, differing from the pre-restart baseline e5168e03-df6d-4e9f-b014-5de4bdfa0688, with a fresh uptime timestamp

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required config
evidence.summary: After reboot, eth1/eth2 addresses (172.20.1.1/24, 172.20.2.1/24) and all forwarding sysctls were present automatically, and the persisted config files were intact, with no manual intervention

evidence.requirement: node2<->node3 path recovered after node1 restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart ping from node2 to 172.20.2.2 (node3) and from node3 to 172.20.1.2 (node2) both succeeded with 0% packet loss
